resources.string: Merges Wi-Fi, mobile signal and battery into a single iPhone-Duo style trio glyph in the status bar.
Master switch. Turn off to restore the stock battery and signal icons.
Which arrangement to draw. The ring is the default; the rectangular one puts a column of signal dots on each side of the centre and a battery bar across the bottom.

Draw the glyph in a window of its own, no longer clipped to the status bar\'s own height (about 43dp), so the whole icon can be shown. The lower part of the glyph then hangs outside the status bar background. Turn off to draw inside the bar again.
Draw the Wi-Fi arcs; the number of arcs follows the real signal level. Turn off to send the stock Wi-Fi icon back to its usual place in the status bar.
Draw four level dots for mobile network signal strength. Turn off to send the stock mobile icon back to its usual place in the status bar.

With no Wi-Fi and not charging, draw two rows of dots instead of one: SIM 1 on top, SIM 2 below. Only applies when both SIMs are present and readable; a single SIM, or while charging, still draws one row for the current data SIM.
Show the battery percentage inside the ring; replaced by a bolt while charging. Turn off to give the charging bolt back to the system as well.
Turn off to drop the bolt from the ring and let the stock charging bolt show next to the battery icon instead.
Where to show the network type label: off, inside the ring, or as a separate icon elsewhere in the status bar.
Where the mobile signal reading lives. Inside the ring keeps the level dots along the bottom of the icon; outside moves it beside the battery icon, in whichever form the switch below selects.

Draw the reading yourself while it is outside the ring: four bars of increasing height for one SIM, a row of dots below them for the other. With a single SIM, only the bars are drawn. Turned off, the system\'s own mobile signal icon is kept.
With two SIMs, draw only the reading of the SIM that carries data and leave the other one out. A single SIM, or one whose data SIM cannot be read, is unaffected.

Overall height of the out-of-ring reading, in dp, so it converts itself to pixels on any screen density. 15dp is the same height as the status bar\'s own signal icon, and is the default; the slider covers 6–20dp. The same row is drawn at the same size whether or not the dot row follows it, so the two shapes never come out different sizes, and pulling the control centre down does not change it.

How far the out-of-ring reading moves sideways in the status bar, in dp; positive moves it right. The default is 0dp and the slider covers -12–12dp. The out-of-ring network type label sits on the reading\'s far side and moves with it.

How far the out-of-ring reading moves up or down in the status bar, in dp; positive moves it down. The default is 0dp and the slider covers -12–12dp. It moves the reading alone and changes neither its height nor the room it reserves.

Enlarge the percentage into the middle of the ring and always keep it there. The Wi-Fi arcs shrink into the top notch, a smaller bolt takes the notch while charging (the arcs are then dropped), and an in-ring network type moves into the notch too.
Pick colors for low battery, charging and critical battery.
Set the color used when the status bar sits on a dark or a light background.
Restore the three state colors to their factory presets.
All three state colors go back to their factory presets; your custom colors will be overwritten.
Switch to the low battery color below this percentage.
Stroke width of the battery ring.
Thickness of the battery bar along the bottom.
Stroke width of the Wi-Fi arcs.
Stroke width of the Wi-Fi arcs, and the vertical position of the group inside the top slot.
Font size of the battery percentage.
Stroke weight of the battery number, 100 lightest to 900 heaviest.
Font size of the 3G/4G/5G label in the ring centre.
Font size of the 3G/4G/5G label shown outside the ring, in the status bar. That label is drawn by the status bar itself, so the matching preview cell here is the only place its size is visible.

The gap between the out-of-ring network type label and its outer side - the one facing away from the battery - in dp. The default is 2dp and the slider covers 0–16dp. Under an RTL language the whole row mirrors and this margin moves to the other side with it.

The gap between the out-of-ring network type label and its inner side - the one facing the battery and the out-of-ring reading - in dp. The default is 2dp and the slider covers 0–16dp. It mirrors under an RTL language too.

When the network type ends in an A (such as 5GA), the size of that trailing A as a percentage of the main label\'s, sharing its baseline. The default is 65%% and the slider covers 50–100%%; 100%% stops the shrink. Applies both inside the ring and outside it.
Stroke weight of the network type, 100 lightest to 900 heaviest.
Opacity of the unlit parts of the glyph.
Write verbose output to the LSPosed log. Enable only when diagnosing.
